pre_registration: These predictions were generated BEFORE any rate-calibration wave saw these points. A calibration wave must be scored against THIS file at THIS git commit. Regenerating this artifact after a calibration and comparing it to itself proves nothing.

benchmarks.citation: Lin, H.-T.V.; Ting, Y.-S.; Ndraha, N.; Hsiao, H.-I.; Sung, W.-C. Effect of Chitosan Incorporation on the Development of Acrylamide during Maillard Reaction in Fructose-Asparagine Model Solution and the Functional Characteristics of the Resultants. Polymers 2022, 14 (8), 1565.

compounds.target_quote: The heating of asparagine-fructose solution for 30 min generated 1859 and 9401 ppb in water and acetic acid, respectively.
compounds.molar_basis: ppb of the reaction solution (ug/L), read off the acrylamide calibration curve built over 0-3125 ppb. The aqueous ('in water') figure is the one used; the 9401 ppb figure is the 1% acetic acid system, which is a different formulation and is NOT scored here.

compounds.target_quote: As HMF can react with asparagine to form MRPs and acrylamide, the production of HMF is probably generated via the caramelization of fructose/glucose (91.56 ppm (Figure 4A) and 34.51 ppm [18]) after heating for 30 min, as compared to HMF generated by the formation of a dicarbonyl intermediate and 3-deoxyglucosone from the Maillard reaction (12.28 ppm (Figure 4A) and 5.13 ppm [18]).
compounds.molar_basis: ppm of the reaction solution, read off an HMF calibration curve built over 0.48-750 ppm; 12.28 ppm = 12280 ppb.

benchmarks.citation: Chang, Y.-W.; Sung, W.-C.; Chen, J.-Y. (Sung, W.-C. et al.) Effect of Hydroxymethylfurfural and Low-Molecular-Weight Chitosan on Formation of Acrylamide and Hydroxymethylfurfural in a Maillard Model System. Polymers 2021, 13 (12), 1901.

compounds.target_quote: 3.3. Effect of Chitosan on Formation of Acrylamide and HMF. Concentration of acrylamide in the solutions containing 0.5% glucose and 0.5% asparagine after 10, 20, and 30 min of heating was 28, 912, and 1459 ppb, respectively (Figure 3B).
compounds.molar_basis: ppb of the reaction solution (ug/L), read off an acrylamide calibration curve built over 0-3125 ppb. Figure 3B is the 1% acetic acid arm; Figure 3A is the deionized-water arm. The two arms are kept in SEPARATE bundles because mixing them is exactly the kind of silent arm-swap this campaign exists to stop.

compounds.target_quote: Glucose-asparagine (0.5%) dissolved in deionized water heated for 30 min generated lower acrylamide (832 ppb) when compared to the glucose-asparagine dissolved in 1% acetic acid (adjusted to pH 6) (Figure 3A,B).

compounds.target_quote: HMF was mainly formed via caramelization of glucose in this study (30 ppm) (Figure 4A) after 30 min of heating compared to that HMF generates through the formation of a dicarbonyl intermediate, 3-deoxyglucosone, from Maillard reaction and caramelization (7 ppm).
compounds.molar_basis: ppm of the reaction solution, read off an HMF calibration curve built over 0.48-750 ppm; 7 ppm = 7000 ppb. The 7 ppm figure is the asparagine+glucose (AG) arm; the 30 ppm figure in the same sentence is the glucose-only (G) arm and is NOT scored here.

benchmarks.citation: Ye, Z.; Xu, H.; Xie, Y.; Peng, Z.; Li, H.; Hou, R.; Cai, H.; Song, W. Tea's Characteristic Components Eliminate Acrylamide in the Maillard Model System. Foods 2024, 13 (17), 2836.

compounds.target_quote: 3.1. The Effects of Instant Green Tea on Acrylamide Levels in the Glc-Asn Model System ... The level of acrylamide under the control condition (i.e., 0 g/mol Asn) was 140.58 +/- 13.92 umol/mol Asn.
compounds.molar_basis: mol of asparagine charged to the reaction. The paper expresses every dose in this study as 'g/mol Asn' and every acrylamide level as 'umol/mol Asn', so asparagine is unambiguously the denominator. Asparagine is also the joint-lowest declared precursor molarity in this bundle (equimolar with glucose), so it is what src/projection._estimate_projection_budget treats as limiting - the paper's denominator and the model's denominator coincide, which is why this pair is unit-commensurable.
